provenance.note: Authored 2026-07-11 from a sanitized operator assignment brief (local, uncommitted) via a grilled design session (grill-with-docs) backed by read-only recon workflow wf_24cbd840-0ff; seven design decisions locked with the operator are recorded as SPEC.md D1-D7.

completionGate.statement: Not achieved until this goal's work ships as a PR driven to mergeable via /yeet (bun run beep yeet: repair -> verify -> publish --pr -> monitor). Each PLAN.md phase is its own PR under this gate.

phases.name: Research: recon, product, architecture, ADR, threat model
phases.exit: research/ holds the recon report, interest taxonomy + seed watchlist, product definition, architecture proposal, technology ADR, and untrusted-ingestion threat model; every SPEC.md deferred decision is resolved or explicitly stopped-and-documented.

phases.name: Proof specification
phases.exit: research/proof-spec.md names scenario, inputs and fixtures, expected authoritative records, expected projections, package ownership, failure cases, invariants, acceptance tests, and explicitly deferred capabilities.

phases.name: Implement first vertical proof
phases.exit: The first vertical proof is implemented per proof-spec.md with deterministic fixtures, no live network or LLM calls in tests, and a sample daily brief generated from fixtures.

phases.name: Verify
phases.exit: Proof tests are green including idempotent reruns, retry behavior, provenance traceability, and projection delete-and-rebuild; repo quality lanes are green for the affected scope.

phases.name: Yeet: PR to mergeable
phases.exit: Each phase PR is open with all required checks green and MERGEABLE.

phases.name: Close
phases.exit: Closeout reflection passes bun run beep lint reflection-artifacts; the staged capability roadmap is recorded; the next vertical proof is recommended with evidence.

stopConditions: Required source files are missing or materially contradictory.
The implementation would exceed named scope.
Verification requires unnamed credentials, cost, destructive side effects, or policy approval.
A step would create difficult-to-reverse package or slice topology before its P0 decision gate is resolved.
A step would introduce a major external dependency or vendor commitment before the technology ADR is accepted.
A step would broaden access to private or privileged data beyond the explicit source allowlist.
A conclusion would conflict with an authoritative repository specification.
The same blocker repeats after reasonable investigation.
